contract.scope: local/test independent synthetic document server; HTTP GET /documents only
contract.policy: unchanged zt-policy-2026.10.1; docs READ grant TTL 60 seconds
contract.authorization: existing /zero-trust/protected-access atomically consumes one-use core grant
contract.handoff: hashed bounded RAM capability, 3 second TTL, one-use GET/path binding; service-authenticated consume
contract.deny_assertion: non-2xx, no protected fixture body hash, zero additional resource deliveries
contract.allow_assertion: 200, exact protected fixture body hash, one additional resource delivery
contract.concurrency: 8 requests share one core grant; exactly one resource delivery
limitations: No production adoption, independent teammate review or high-load SLA assertion
Core grant consumption is authorization point; revocation does not cancel an already authorized in-flight request
No atomic transaction spanning core journal and business action; delivery failure does not refund a consumed grant
Local internal HTTP only; production TLS/mTLS, OIDC/IdP mapping, HA and resource streaming are not validated

conditions.network: internal Docker networks; no published ports
conditions.timing: client HTTP duration inside container; excludes Docker exec startup
conditions.all_service_network_hops: mTLS, including native core and monitoring

transport_contract.scope: NGINX C02 PEP bridge to existing core API through dedicated mTLS gateway
transport_contract.tls: TLS 1.2 minimum; chain, EKU, time, server DNS name, SHA-256 leaf pins
transport_contract.identity: Exact client certificate fingerprint to server-owned service identity; request header identity ignored
transport_contract.authorization: Service path scope AND existing application API-key role/tenant/session checks
transport_contract.rotation: Explicit overlap and retirement; fresh TLS contexts and per-request peer policy reload; no HTTP fallback
transport_contract.keys: CA private keys RAM only; leaf private keys RAM and own 0600 Linux volumes only; no host key files
transport_contract.network: All internal; no host ports/socket; bridge has no plaintext core network route

all_hops_contract.scope: selected local NGINX/Prometheus/Alertmanager graph; historical HTTP comparisons are separate
hops: authenticated management probes -> native TLS endpoints
all_hops_contract.verification: CA/time/EKU/hostname validation; exact leaf/service pin at Python endpoints; verified CA/SAN identities at native Go endpoints and NGINX upstreams
excluded: external public release downloads (HTTPS + pinned SHA256, no client-cert authority)
production deployment, automated CA/CRL/OCSP/HA and policy rollback protection

certificate_contract.scope: selected local mTLS graph; workload leaf certificate issuance/renewal with step-ca
certificate_contract.publication: single-writer journal; overlap pins, atomic same-key leaf replacement, reload ack and native TLS observations, old-pin retirement
certificate_contract.test_lifetimes: normal 20 minutes, canaries 30 seconds; accelerated renewal thresholds only for local tests
deferred: production deployment and real workload attestation
per-workload private-key custody, rekey and root/intermediate rotation
HSM/external secret manager/HA and independent reproduction
distributed concurrent policy writers and policy anti-rollback
active CRL/OCSP, immediate native Go connection revocation, certificate-specific production alerts

summary.scope: Repeated functional assertions, not unique scenario count, latency SLA or detection quality score

execution_context.performed_by: Codex tool-assisted execution in Chaeheeju's infrastructure scope
execution_context.shared_background: Existing Docker cluster preserved; load uncontrolled; no performance comparison
execution_context.integration_private_material: Offline root and bootstrap provisioner keys RAM only; encrypted issuer/password/DB in owned Linux CA volume; leaf/delegated server-signing keys RAM/owned Linux volumes 0600, no host private files/OS trust change
execution_context.server_renewal_authorization: Registered control-plane-only JWK key, fixed server identity/SAN/serverAuth and CSR-bound JWT. No own-root X5C provisioner in final profile.
execution_context.key_and_ca_lifetimes: same-key workload renewal, server 20m, management identity 1h, test canary 30s; root/issuer/rekey/HSM/HA/CA API granular RBAC deferred

preliminary_notes: Pilot first status RPC exited before generation-zero status existed; initialization now publishes status before concurrent issuance.
ServerAuth-only /renew was rejected by actual CA with incompatible key usage; server leaf purpose was preserved and reissuance was separated.

An X5C prototype first missed its provisioner audience fragment; corrected prototype passed one full trial but was deliberately stopped for authorization review. It is not the final implementation or a completed two-repeat result.

Source review found broader CA management capabilities of own-root X5C. Final profile uses explicitly registered, control-plane-only JWK signing keys. Ordinary clients cannot issue target server certificates or revoke other identities.
An initial unit expected ValueError on a wrong issuer; signature failures are now classified as a safe lifecycle rejection, and the final full suites passed.
